title: Axiom-ZSpace: A Blind-Search, Gate-Logic Transit Detection Pipeline with a Measured Threshold Catalog
description:
Axiom-ZSpace is a blind-search, gate-logic transit detection pipeline for TESS and Kepler that treats code as an instrument. The pipeline executes ingestion → BLS (ladder, FAP firewall) → ephemeris → audits → 11-gate ruling engine (circuit breaker) → CVS with every tunable constant centralized in config/production.yaml → thresholds.py. Each verdict carries a complete, auditable proof chain.

The code is organized as six explicit stages with clear contracts (ingestion, detectors, ephemeris, auditors, validator, core). All 11 gates, the FAP firewall, ladder (k20) and CVS weights live in one file with per-key evidence in THRESHOLDS_REPORT.md. The 101-test offline suite enforces determinism, circuit breaker, and ephemeris identity as executable contracts.

Measured as an instrument: controlled synthetic BIG400 (400 true + 400 false, 8 seeds) yields 41.2% recall at correct period, 81.7% precision, 4.25% contamination FPR; real Kepler 12+12 yields 41.7% recall. Thresholds are not tuned — they are measured.

Verification: 101 tests (python -m pytest tests/ -q, offline). Where a supplementary C99 port exists (mechanically derived via Purce), it is checked: 148/148 validator kernels at 1e-9 and 90/90 synthetic cards at 2e-3. BIG400 Python 400/400 is the versioned evidence.

Performance — CPUs as Efficient Alternatives to GPU Acceleration: As a supplementary artifact, the same logic achieves 42.8 ms/TIC (650× vs Python 27.8 s, 40.6× per-core) on 3k-point curves on a commodity 16-core CPU (-O3 -march=native -flto -ffast-math -fopenmp-simd, Ubuntu 22.04, gcc 11.4). For context, GTLS on RTX 4090 reports 15.7× vs TLS; benchmarking the C99 artifact on CPU shows a portable, bit-identical derivation can exceed GPU throughputs when the bottleneck is gate logic. Throughput is a consequence, not the claim.

Source: https://github.com/Zierax/Axiom-Zspace (tag v1.1.1) — zspace_engine/, C99-Version/ (supplementary), paper/JOSS/paper.md + paper.bib archived with tag. License: MIT. Archived on Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22255875.

This record describes the Axiom-ZSpace software itself — its architecture, reproducibility guarantees, and supplementary C99 artifact — rather than novel astrophysical results.
notes: JOSS paper: paper/JOSS/paper.md + paper.tex + paper.bib + paper.pdf (4pp, 05 Sep 2026, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22255875). 101 tests, BIG400 41.2%/4.25%, 148/148 at 1e-9 (Purce slight). Code as instrument.
